title: Taste and See That the Lord Is Good
summary: Jesus isn't cheering from the sidelines. He is with you in the trial, and those who look to him will never be ashamed.
exhortation: Whatever you're doing this morning, on your way to work or school, our desire is that God will bless you through this time and remind you of his grace in your life: that he is with us no matter what.

In this psalm the Lord tells us he is with us through our trials and difficulties, not simply that he will take them away. Are you going through something hard? Jesus isn't cheering you on from the sidelines, saying, "Go for it. You can do it." He is with you through it all. The pain you feel, he feels. Your fatigue and frustration, he feels as well.

Sometimes we feel like the Lord isn't with us because things are hard, but nothing could be further from the truth. "I sought the Lord, and he answered me and delivered me from all my fears." When things are difficult, we need to go straight to God with our fears, not retreat. We will never be ashamed when we put our trust in Jesus, because he is completely trustworthy.

So as we worship this morning, our goal is to take refuge in the one who is faithful to the end, through the hardest times, and who will never leave us or forsake us. Let's taste and see this morning that the Lord is good.
prayer: Lord God, we fix our eyes on you as we start our day. Be fixed in our view. We're tempted to just go about our day like the man in James who says, "I'll go to that city and make some money and do whatever I do." That can take over, and we don't want it.
May our eyes be fixed on you alone. May we see that our hope is only Jesus. Amen.
